verdict: Neither is the other's better version. ChatGPT is the wider, more consumer-friendly product: stronger multimodal input, a deeper integration story, and a free tier that is actually useful. Claude is the stronger choice for long-form work and for strict instruction-following, and its top tier costs more. Pick the one that matches the shape of your daily work, not the one with the better benchmark.
body:
Side-by-side

ChatGPT (OpenAI) Claude (Anthropic)
Free tierYes, genuinely usableYes, lighter limits
Consumer paid tier$20 / month (Plus)$20 / month (Pro)
Top consumer tier$200 / month (Pro)$100–200 / month (Max)
Context windowStrong, degrades on very long inputsLargest in class, holds structure
Multimodal inputText, audio, image in one conversationText and image; no consumer voice
Instruction-followingStrong on everyday tasksMost literal on multi-step constraints
Coding agentsIntegrated assistantClaude Code / Cowork are the strongest in the set
Ecosystem depthDeeper: more integrations, wider tool setNarrower, more focused

Where ChatGPT wins

On everyday speed and on the sheer breadth of what you can do without leaving the window, ChatGPT still leads. Its multimodal input — voice plus image in one conversation — is the most complete in the consumer set, and its integration story is deeper: a wider tool set and more add-ons. If your work is a mix of quick drafts, image-understanding and the occasional coding task, it is the better all-rounder.

Where Claude wins

On long-form work and on instruction-following, Claude is the stronger tool. The context window is larger and holds structure better, which is the reason many developers migrate specifically to stop hitting the ceiling. And on the agentic side — Claude Code and Claude Cowork — it is the most capable in-ecosystem coding and task-delegation set on the market. If your dominant task is a long document or a strict multi-step constraint, this is the one to pick.

The cost question

At the entry point the two are tied at $20 a month. They diverge at the top tier: ChatGPT's $200 Pro tier is a single step, while Claude splits its upper range across a $100 and a $200 Max. For a heavy daily user the Claude Max is the more flexible option, but you pay more for it. The honest answer is to stay on Pro on either side until it genuinely bottlenecks you, and only then move up.

Pick by scenario

If your main work is…PickWhy
A mix of quick drafts, image questions and short codingChatGPTThe wider all-rounder with the better free tier
Long documents, transcripts or a large codebaseClaudeThe context window holds structure that the other one loses
Strict multi-step instructions with hard constraintsClaudeMost literal on the constraints
Terminal-based coding or task delegationClaudeThe strongest in-ecosystem agent set
A team that wants the most integrationsChatGPTDeeper ecosystem and wider tool set

Running both is a legitimate strategy

A lot of professional users keep one for everyday work and the other for the long-form task that justifies the second subscription. The cost of doing that is roughly $40 a month — less than one day of a consultant, and less than the cost of using the wrong tool on the wrong task.
